comparison: Strong agreement on CNN foothold prediction findings (C18, C30, C31). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with high confidence. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate train-test splits and AUC metrics, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'strong' results and accepted methodology without critique.

Significant disagreement on leg length findings (C56, C57, C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite noting small sample size, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN with substantial doubts about statistical artifacts, correlations of correlations, and whether dimensionless measures can demonstrate scale effects.

Major disagreement on energetic cost interpretation (C19, C36-C43). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong quantitative evidence, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning the validity of comparing human tortuous paths to simulated straight paths as 'not an apples-to-apples comparison' and preferring more cautious conclusions.

Strong agreement on tortuosity-slope relationship (C20, C45-C49, C53-C55). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes comprehensive quantitative characterization with modest correlations, while peer reviewers consider this the 'strongest' evidence and a 'considerable strength' despite finding it 'hardly surprising.'

Strong agreement on methodological contributions (C61, C62, C81). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes improvements over prior work and reasonable inference about general utility, while peer reviewers unanimously praised the 'impressive' technical achievement and workflow as opening new approaches to studying natural behavior.

Partial disagreement on planning claims (C2, C4-C6, C72-C73, C80). OpenEval rates summary claims as SUPPORTED by quantitative findings, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting conclusions remain 'more suggestive' and that specific mechanisms and visual features used in decision processes remain unclear.

Strong agreement on reconstruction accuracy validation (C23-C26, C28). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation with appropriate context and sound methodology, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the 'methodologically very impressive' technical achievement without questioning the reconstruction reliability data.

Weak overlap on individual path analysis (C59). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for slope-tortuosity relationship at individual path level, while peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating for R5 focuses on leg length correlations (C56-C58) with only tangential connection to C59.

OpenEval rates energetic optimization claims (C64-C68) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation without direct energetic measurements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims, though peer R3 questions related energetic interpretations.

OpenEval rates planning horizon claims (C74-C79) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about reconciling discrepancies between studies without direct measurement. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims.

OpenEval rates methodological documentation (C85-C98) as SUPPORTED, noting comprehensive technical specifications and sound synchronization approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological details.

OpenEval rates off-path gaze claims (C100-C103) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about functional role without quantitative analysis linking gaze to turning decisions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these claims.

OpenEval rates characterization of field gaps (C1, C7-C8, C10, C13, C63) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate representation of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these contextual claims.

OpenEval rates citations of prior work (C9, C11-C12, C14-C17, C21, C32-C33, C35, C44, C65-C67) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate and relevant citations providing essential context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these citation claims.
